questions.prompt: In 6/8 time, how many main beats are normally felt in one bar?
options: Two dotted crotchet beats
Six minim beats
Three semibreve beats
One quaver beat
questions.correctAnswer: Two dotted crotchet beats
questions.explanation: 6/8 is compound duple time, so the six quavers are normally felt as two dotted crotchet beats.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify beat groupings in compound time signatures.

questions.prompt: How many semiquavers equal one dotted quaver?
options: Three
Two
Four
Six
questions.correctAnswer: Three
questions.explanation: A dotted quaver equals a quaver plus half its value, which is three semiquavers.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate dotted notes to equivalent shorter note values.

questions.prompt: Which degree of a major scale is called the dominant?
options: Fifth degree
Second degree
Sixth degree
Seventh degree
questions.correctAnswer: Fifth degree
questions.explanation: The dominant is the fifth degree of a major or minor scale and strongly leads back to the tonic.
questions.learningOutcome: Name functional degrees of major and minor scales.

questions.prompt: What change creates the harmonic minor scale from the natural minor scale?
options: Raise the seventh degree
Lower the third degree
Raise the fourth degree
Remove the leading note
questions.correctAnswer: Raise the seventh degree
questions.explanation: The harmonic minor scale raises the seventh degree to create a stronger leading note to the tonic.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish natural and harmonic minor scale forms.

questions.prompt: What is the relative minor of C major?
options: A minor
C minor
E minor
G minor
questions.correctAnswer: A minor
questions.explanation: A minor shares the same key signature as C major, with no sharps or flats.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify relative major and minor keys from key signatures.

questions.prompt: Which chord movement forms a perfect cadence?
options: V to I
IV to I
I to V
ii to IV
questions.correctAnswer: V to I
questions.explanation: A perfect cadence moves from the dominant chord to the tonic chord and gives a strong sense of closure.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common cadences by chord movement.

questions.prompt: A basic triad is built from which three chord tones?
options: Root, third, and fifth
Root, second, and fourth
Third, sixth, and seventh
Second, fifth, and octave
questions.correctAnswer: Root, third, and fifth
questions.explanation: A triad stacks two thirds above a root, producing the root, third, and fifth.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the chord tones that form major and minor triads.

questions.prompt: In alto clef, which staff line represents middle C?
options: The third line
The first line
The fourth line
The fifth line
questions.correctAnswer: The third line
questions.explanation: The alto clef is a C clef that places middle C on the middle, or third, line of the staff.
questions.learningOutcome: Read pitch positions in treble, bass, and alto clefs.

questions.prompt: What does a staccato mark tell a performer to do?
options: Play the note short and detached
Play the note gradually louder
Hold the note longer than written
Repeat the whole section from the start
questions.correctAnswer: Play the note short and detached
questions.explanation: Staccato articulation shortens and separates notes without changing their written pitch.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common articulation marks in performance.

questions.prompt: What does crescendo mean in a musical score?
options: Gradually becoming louder
Gradually becoming slower
Suddenly becoming silent
Repeating softly from the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: Gradually becoming louder
questions.explanation: Crescendo is a dynamic instruction that asks performers to increase volume gradually.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply common dynamic terms and symbols in performance.

questions.prompt: Which family best describes the nyatiti used by Luo musicians?
options: Lyre
Trumpet
Xylophone
Flute
questions.correctAnswer: Lyre
questions.explanation: The nyatiti is an eight-string lyre traditionally associated with Luo music making.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify selected Kenyan indigenous instruments by type and community context.

questions.prompt: Which term best classifies the kayamba when it is played by shaking?
options: Idiophone
Aerophone
Chordophone
Membranophone
questions.correctAnswer: Idiophone
questions.explanation: A kayamba produces sound through the vibration of its own body and seeds, so it is an idiophone.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify instruments using standard sound-production categories.

questions.prompt: What information does a key signature give at the beginning of a staff?
options: The sharps or flats normally used in the key
The exact tempo of every bar
The number of performers required
The title of the composition
questions.correctAnswer: The sharps or flats normally used in the key
questions.explanation: A key signature places sharps or flats after the clef to show the tonal centre and expected accidentals.
questions.learningOutcome: Read and interpret common key signatures.

questions.prompt: In music enterprise, what does copyright mainly protect?
options: Original musical works and related creative rights
Only the colour of an album cover
Every public-domain folk melody forever
A performer's school timetable
questions.correctAnswer: Original musical works and related creative rights
questions.explanation: Copyright protects original creative works and helps creators control use, copying, performance, and distribution.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain basic copyright rights and responsibilities in music.

questions.prompt: What does DAW stand for in music production?
options: Digital Audio Workstation
Dynamic Acoustic Writing
Direct Amplifier Wave
Dance Arrangement Workshop
questions.correctAnswer: Digital Audio Workstation
questions.explanation: A Digital Audio Workstation is software used to record, edit, arrange, and mix music.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common digital tools used in music recording and editing.

questions.prompt: Why is 9/8 described as compound triple time?
options: It has three main beats, each dividing into three quavers
It has nine separate crotchet beats
It always has three bars in each phrase
It can only be played by three instruments
questions.correctAnswer: It has three main beats, each dividing into three quavers
questions.explanation: The nine quavers in 9/8 are normally grouped as three dotted crotchet beats.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how compound time signatures group beats and subdivisions.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes syncopation?
options: Emphasis placed on weak beats or offbeats
A melody sung only in unison
A chord built only from perfect fifths
A tempo that never changes
questions.correctAnswer: Emphasis placed on weak beats or offbeats
questions.explanation: Syncopation shifts accent away from expected strong beats and creates rhythmic tension.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe rhythmic devices used in composition and performance.

questions.prompt: How is a tie different from a slur?
options: A tie joins same-pitch notes into one longer sound
A tie marks notes to be played more loudly
A tie connects different pitches smoothly
A tie changes a major key to minor
questions.correctAnswer: A tie joins same-pitch notes into one longer sound
questions.explanation: A tie extends the duration of notes with the same pitch, while a slur groups different notes for smooth articulation.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish common notation marks and their performance meanings.

questions.prompt: What is an anacrusis in a melody?
options: A pickup note or notes before the first full bar
A chord written only at the final cadence
A rest that cancels the time signature
A repeated bass note throughout a piece
questions.correctAnswer: A pickup note or notes before the first full bar
questions.explanation: An anacrusis leads into the first complete measure and is often balanced by a shortened final bar.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify structural features used at the opening of melodies.

questions.prompt: In compound time, how does each main beat usually divide?
options: Into three equal parts
Into two unequal parts
Into four bars
Into one whole note only
questions.correctAnswer: Into three equal parts
questions.explanation: Compound beats are dotted beats that naturally divide into three equal subdivisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare simple and compound beat subdivision.

questions.prompt: Which scale form raises the sixth and seventh degrees when ascending in common classical practice?
options: Melodic minor
Natural minor
Whole-tone scale
Major pentatonic
questions.correctAnswer: Melodic minor
questions.explanation: The melodic minor form commonly raises the sixth and seventh degrees ascending to create smoother melodic motion.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the construction and use of melodic minor scales.

questions.prompt: Which notes form a dominant seventh chord from root position?
options: Root, third, fifth, and minor seventh
Root, second, fourth, and sixth
Root, fourth, fifth, and octave
Third, fifth, sixth, and major seventh
questions.correctAnswer: Root, third, fifth, and minor seventh
questions.explanation: A dominant seventh chord is a major triad with an added minor seventh above the root.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the structure of dominant seventh chords.

questions.prompt: In first inversion, which note of a triad is in the bass?
options: The third
The root
The fifth
The seventh
questions.correctAnswer: The third
questions.explanation: A first-inversion triad places the third of the chord as the lowest sounding note.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify triad inversions from the bass note.

questions.prompt: Which chord movement forms a plagal cadence?
options: IV to I
V to I
I to ii
vi to iii
questions.correctAnswer: IV to I
questions.explanation: A plagal cadence moves from the subdominant chord to the tonic chord.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare perfect, plagal, imperfect, and interrupted cadences.

questions.prompt: What is the main effect of an imperfect cadence?
options: It leaves the phrase feeling unfinished on the dominant
It gives final closure on the tonic
It changes every note into a triplet
It removes the need for harmony
questions.correctAnswer: It leaves the phrase feeling unfinished on the dominant
questions.explanation: An imperfect cadence ends on chord V, creating a pause that expects continuation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how cadence choice affects phrase direction.

questions.prompt: A B flat clarinet sounds how when compared with its written pitch?
options: A major second lower
A perfect fifth higher
The same pitch
An octave and a third lower
questions.correctAnswer: A major second lower
questions.explanation: A written C on a B flat clarinet sounds as concert B flat, which is a major second lower.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the sounding relationship of common transposing instruments.

questions.prompt: What is a practical use of the circle of fifths?
options: Finding related keys and key signatures
Measuring stage lighting levels
Counting performers in a choir
Changing every melody into a drum pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Finding related keys and key signatures
questions.explanation: The circle of fifths shows relationships among keys and the order of sharps and flats.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the circle of fifths to understand related keys.

questions.prompt: How many different pitch classes are used in a pentatonic scale?
options: Five
Four
Seven
Twelve
questions.correctAnswer: Five
questions.explanation: The word pentatonic refers to a five-note scale, common in many folk and popular music traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify scale types used in classroom composition and cultural music.

questions.prompt: Which description best matches homophonic texture?
options: One main melody supported by accompaniment
Several unrelated melodies at the same time
Only unpitched percussion sounds
Complete silence between every note
questions.correctAnswer: One main melody supported by accompaniment
questions.explanation: Homophony features a clear principal melody with harmonic or rhythmic support.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify musical textures in written descriptions and scores.

questions.prompt: What happens in antiphonal singing?
options: Two groups or voices answer each other
All singers remain silent while drums play
One person sings without any response
Every phrase is sung backwards
questions.correctAnswer: Two groups or voices answer each other
questions.explanation: Antiphonal performance uses alternation between groups, soloists, or sections.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ensemble techniques used in choral and community music.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes call and response?
options: A leader sings or plays a phrase and a group answers
A soloist repeats scales without accompaniment
The audience leaves before a song ends
A performer changes instruments after every beat
questions.correctAnswer: A leader sings or plays a phrase and a group answers
questions.explanation: Call and response creates musical dialogue and is common in many African performance traditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain participatory structures in African music making.

questions.prompt: What is polyrhythm?
options: Two or more contrasting rhythms performed together
One long note held without change
A melody using only two pitches
A chord progression without rhythm
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more contrasting rhythms performed together
questions.explanation: Polyrhythm layers different rhythmic patterns so they interact within the same pulse.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe layered rhythmic practices in African and contemporary music.

questions.prompt: What is an ostinato?
options: A repeated musical pattern
A sudden change of clef
A silent rehearsal instruction
A scale with no tonic
questions.correctAnswer: A repeated musical pattern
questions.explanation: An ostinato is a repeated rhythm, melody, or harmonic pattern that can organize a composition.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify repeated devices used to build musical structure.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a drone in music?
options: A sustained or repeated pitch supporting the melody
A final page of lyrics
A tempo marking meaning fast
A group of unrelated accidentals
questions.correctAnswer: A sustained or repeated pitch supporting the melody
questions.explanation: A drone provides a continuous tonal reference, often on the tonic or dominant.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe accompaniment devices used in folk and contemporary arrangements.

questions.prompt: What is one main responsibility of a conductor during ensemble performance?
options: Giving tempo, entries, cutoffs, and expressive cues
Writing every performer's examination number
Replacing all instrumental parts with lyrics
Changing the key after each bar without warning
questions.correctAnswer: Giving tempo, entries, cutoffs, and expressive cues
questions.explanation: A conductor coordinates timing, starts, endings, balance, dynamics, and interpretation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of conducting gestures in ensemble coordination.

questions.prompt: Why should vocalists warm up before a demanding rehearsal?
options: To prepare the voice and reduce strain
To make written notation unnecessary
To guarantee perfect pitch without practice
To replace breathing technique with volume
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare the voice and reduce strain
questions.explanation: Warm-ups support healthy tone production, breath control, range, and focus before singing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply healthy vocal preparation habits in rehearsal and performance.

questions.prompt: What kind of data is usually carried by MIDI?
options: Performance instructions such as pitch, duration, velocity, and controller changes
Only final stereo audio waves
Printed lyrics and copyright certificates
Microphone cable resistance readings
questions.correctAnswer: Performance instructions such as pitch, duration, velocity, and controller changes
questions.explanation: MIDI stores and transmits musical performance information rather than recorded sound waves.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how MIDI differs from digital audio recording.

questions.prompt: What does quantization do in a DAW?
options: Aligns recorded MIDI or audio events to a rhythmic grid
Changes a singer's language automatically
Deletes all rests from a score
Prints a copyright licence
questions.correctAnswer: Aligns recorded MIDI or audio events to a rhythmic grid
questions.explanation: Quantization corrects timing by moving notes or events closer to selected beat divisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Use basic editing concepts to improve timing in digital production.

questions.prompt: Which action best respects a community song used in a school arrangement?
options: Acknowledge the source community and use the song respectfully
Claim the song was invented alone by the arranger
Change sacred words for comedy without consultation
Remove all cultural context from the performance notes
questions.correctAnswer: Acknowledge the source community and use the song respectfully
questions.explanation: Responsible arrangement credits sources, respects meaning, and avoids misuse of cultural material.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate respectful use of community music in learning projects.

questions.prompt: Which item is most important in a simple programme note for a school music performance?
options: Brief context, performers, title, and what listeners should notice
Private phone numbers of all performers
A list of unrelated sports results
Only the price of every instrument used
questions.correctAnswer: Brief context, performers, title, and what listeners should notice
questions.explanation: Programme notes help an audience understand the work, performers, context, and listening focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare informative notes for classroom and public performances.

questions.prompt: Which note grouping correctly fills a bar of 6/8 time?
options: One dotted crotchet plus three quavers
Three crotchets plus one minim
Two semibreves plus one quaver
Five crotchets and a rest
questions.correctAnswer: One dotted crotchet plus three quavers
questions.explanation: A 6/8 bar contains six quavers, so a dotted crotchet and three quavers make the full bar.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply compound-time values to complete bars accurately.

questions.prompt: A composer wants a dance feel with two strong beats per bar, each subdivided into three. Which time signature fits best?
questions.explanation: 6/8 has two dotted crotchet beats, and each beat divides into three quavers.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable time signatures for intended rhythmic character.

questions.prompt: In an ensemble, one player repeats three equal notes while another fits two equal notes into the same beat span. What device is being used?
options: A 3:2 cross-rhythm
A perfect cadence
A chromatic scale
A first-inversion triad
questions.correctAnswer: A 3:2 cross-rhythm
questions.explanation: A 3:2 cross-rhythm layers three pulses against two pulses within the same time span.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply rhythmic layering concepts to African and contemporary ensemble patterns.

questions.prompt: Which revision would make a syncopated rhythm clearer in notation?
options: Tie notes across weak and strong beat positions while preserving the bar value
Remove all bar lines and time signatures
Write every note as a semibreve regardless of pulse
Place accidentals before every rest
questions.correctAnswer: Tie notes across weak and strong beat positions while preserving the bar value
questions.explanation: Syncopation is often notated with ties that show accents continuing across expected beat positions.
questions.learningOutcome: Notate rhythmic displacement accurately within a chosen meter.

questions.prompt: A melody in G major is transposed up a whole tone. Which new key is expected?
options: A major
F major
E minor
C major
questions.correctAnswer: A major
questions.explanation: Moving every note of G major up a whole tone gives A major, which has three sharps.
questions.learningOutcome: Transpose melodies by interval and adjust key signatures correctly.

questions.prompt: What is the relative minor of E flat major?
options: C minor
E minor
G minor
B flat minor
questions.correctAnswer: C minor
questions.explanation: C minor shares E flat major's key signature of three flats.
questions.learningOutcome: Use key signatures to find relative minor keys.

questions.prompt: Which notes form the dominant triad in D major?
options: A, C sharp, and E
D, F sharp, and A
G, B, and D
B, D, and F sharp
questions.correctAnswer: A, C sharp, and E
questions.explanation: The dominant in D major is built on A, and the A major triad contains A, C sharp, and E.
questions.learningOutcome: Build primary triads in major keys.

questions.prompt: Which progression best represents a cadential six-four leading to a perfect cadence in C major?
options: I64 to V to I
IV to ii to vi
I to iii to IV
vi to V to ii
questions.correctAnswer: I64 to V to I
questions.explanation: A cadential six-four decorates the dominant before resolving through V to the tonic.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply common cadential patterns in harmonisation.

questions.prompt: At the end of a phrase in C major, which chord pair would best support a perfect cadence?
options: G major followed by C major
F major followed by A minor
C major followed by D minor
A minor followed by E minor
questions.correctAnswer: G major followed by C major
questions.explanation: In C major, G major is chord V and C major is chord I, forming V to I.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose chord progressions that fit phrase endings.

questions.prompt: In four-part harmony, why are consecutive perfect fifths usually avoided in strict writing?
options: They weaken the independence of the voice parts
They always change the time signature
They make the harmony legally protected
They force every voice into alto clef
questions.correctAnswer: They weaken the independence of the voice parts
questions.explanation: Parallel fifths can make two voices sound fused, reducing the independence expected in four-part harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic voice-leading conventions in four-part harmony.

questions.prompt: A C major triad is written in first inversion. Which note should be in the bass?
options: E, the third of the chord
C, the root of the chord
G, the fifth of the chord
B, the leading note
questions.correctAnswer: E, the third of the chord
questions.explanation: First inversion places the third of the chord in the bass, and E is the third of C major.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inversion rules when arranging triads.

questions.prompt: In C major, how should the leading note B normally resolve in a final cadence?
options: Upward to C
Downward to A
Sideways to another B
Downward to F
questions.correctAnswer: Upward to C
questions.explanation: The leading note is a semitone below the tonic and normally resolves upward to the tonic in tonal harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Resolve tendency tones appropriately in tonal cadences.

questions.prompt: A piece in C major modulates to the dominant key. Which new key is most likely established?
options: G major
F major
A minor
E flat major
questions.correctAnswer: G major
questions.explanation: The dominant key of C major is G major, often confirmed by F sharp and a cadence in G.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify closely related keys used in simple modulation.

questions.prompt: When setting English text to music, which choice usually supports natural word stress?
options: Place strong syllables on strong beats
Place every syllable on the last beat only
Ignore punctuation and phrase shape
Use one pitch for all emotional words
questions.correctAnswer: Place strong syllables on strong beats
questions.explanation: Good text setting respects natural speech rhythm by aligning important syllables with musical accents.
questions.learningOutcome: Set words to melody using natural stress and phrase shape.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows word painting?
options: A rising melodic line on the word climb
A silent bar after every noun
A key signature copied from another song
A drum pattern replacing all lyrics
questions.correctAnswer: A rising melodic line on the word climb
questions.explanation: Word painting matches musical shape to the meaning of the text.
questions.learningOutcome: Use melodic and rhythmic choices to reflect meaning in lyrics.

questions.prompt: A learner arranges a folk song for voice, drum, and kayamba. Which accompaniment choice is most suitable?
options: Keep a steady pulse and leave space for the vocal call and response
Cover every vocal phrase with loud continuous drumming
Change the tempo randomly in each line
Remove all repeated patterns from the arrangement
questions.correctAnswer: Keep a steady pulse and leave space for the vocal call and response
questions.explanation: Effective accompaniment supports the song's structure, dance pulse, and vocal interaction without overpowering them.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange accompaniment that supports traditional song features.

questions.prompt: When arranging a song for mixed voices, what should be checked first?
options: Whether each part sits within a comfortable vocal range
Whether all parts use the same highest note
Whether the bass line copies the soprano exactly
Whether every singer changes clef every bar
questions.correctAnswer: Whether each part sits within a comfortable vocal range
questions.explanation: Vocal ranges affect tone, accuracy, health, and balance in choral writing.
questions.learningOutcome: Write and adapt vocal parts for suitable ranges.

questions.prompt: A choir repeatedly sings flat near the end of phrases. Which rehearsal focus is most likely to help?
options: Breath support, listening to the tonal centre, and tuning sustained notes
Singing louder without listening
Removing all phrase endings
Changing every note into percussion claps
questions.correctAnswer: Breath support, listening to the tonal centre, and tuning sustained notes
questions.explanation: Flat singing often improves when singers manage breath, hear harmonic context, and tune important sustained pitches.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply rehearsal strategies to improve ensemble tuning.

questions.prompt: During a rehearsal, the accompaniment hides the solo melody. What is the best musical adjustment?
options: Reduce accompaniment volume and texture so the melody is clear
Ask the soloist to stop singing permanently
Add more instruments to play over the melody
Ignore balance until the final performance
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce accompaniment volume and texture so the melody is clear
questions.explanation: Good ensemble balance lets important melodic material be heard without unnecessary force.
questions.learningOutcome: Adjust ensemble texture and dynamics for clear presentation.

questions.prompt: A microphone feeds back during a school performance. Which response should be tried first?
options: Move the microphone away from the loudspeaker path and reduce gain
Point the microphone directly at the loudspeaker
Turn every monitor to maximum volume
Cover the microphone with paper while singing
questions.correctAnswer: Move the microphone away from the loudspeaker path and reduce gain
questions.explanation: Feedback occurs when amplified sound re-enters the microphone, so position and gain control are important.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe sound reinforcement practices during performance.

questions.prompt: A recorded vocal sounds muddy because low frequencies are too strong. Which mix action is most suitable?
options: Reduce unnecessary low frequencies with equalization
Add more low bass to every track
Export the track without listening
Delete all high-frequency instruments
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce unnecessary low frequencies with equalization
questions.explanation: Equalization can reduce excessive low-frequency energy and improve clarity.
questions.learningOutcome: Use basic mixing decisions to improve clarity in recorded music.

questions.prompt: Which form is represented by a first section, contrasting middle section, and return of the first section?
options: Ternary form
Binary form
Through-composed form
Strophic form only
questions.correctAnswer: Ternary form
questions.explanation: Ternary form is commonly described as ABA, with a return after contrast.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common forms from sectional descriptions.

questions.prompt: In theme and variations, what normally remains recognisable?
options: The original theme's identity
Only the concert ticket price
The microphone brand
A completely unrelated melody each time
questions.correctAnswer: The original theme's identity
questions.explanation: Variations change features such as rhythm, harmony, texture, or ornamentation while keeping the theme identifiable.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how composers vary a musical idea while preserving identity.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits rondo form?
options: A recurring main theme alternates with contrasting episodes
A melody is sung once with no return
Every performer improvises a different tempo
Only two identical sections are allowed
questions.correctAnswer: A recurring main theme alternates with contrasting episodes
questions.explanation: Rondo form uses a returning refrain, often labelled A, between contrasting sections.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize recurring-theme structures in instrumental music.

questions.prompt: Which sequence names the main large sections of sonata form?
options: Exposition, development, and recapitulation
Warm-up, rehearsal, and transport
Verse, bridge, and invoice
Scale, arpeggio, and copyright
questions.correctAnswer: Exposition, development, and recapitulation
questions.explanation: Sonata form usually presents themes, develops them, and returns them in a recapitulation.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline major formal sections in selected Western classical forms.

questions.prompt: Which set of details would make field documentation of a Kenyan folk song most useful?
options: Community context, function, lyrics translation, instruments, dance, and permission notes
Only the recorder's favourite colour
A list of unrelated pop songs
A random tempo marking without source information
questions.correctAnswer: Community context, function, lyrics translation, instruments, dance, and permission notes
questions.explanation: Good documentation records musical, cultural, and ethical information so the song can be studied responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Document music practices with attention to context, meaning, and consent.

questions.prompt: A class adapts a community song for a school event. Which step shows ethical practice?
options: Seek guidance where needed and credit the source tradition in the programme
Remove all references to the source community
Present the song as newly invented by the class
Use sacred material casually without checking meaning
questions.correctAnswer: Seek guidance where needed and credit the source tradition in the programme
questions.explanation: Ethical adaptation respects ownership, meaning, permission, and attribution.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ethical decision making when adapting cultural music.

questions.prompt: Which elements are most useful when recording a dance sequence for rehearsal notes?
options: Counts, pathways, formations, gestures, and phrase structure
Only costume colours and snack prices
Every performer's unrelated exam marks
The serial numbers of the speakers
questions.correctAnswer: Counts, pathways, formations, gestures, and phrase structure
questions.explanation: Dance rehearsal notes should capture timing, movement direction, grouping, and expression.
questions.learningOutcome: Document dance movement for accurate rehearsal and performance.

questions.prompt: Which criteria best support a fair evaluation of a vocal ensemble performance?
options: Intonation, rhythm, diction, balance, expression, and stage discipline
Only the number of costumes on stage
The height of the loudspeaker stands
The popularity of the first performer
questions.correctAnswer: Intonation, rhythm, diction, balance, expression, and stage discipline
questions.explanation: Performance evaluation should focus on musical accuracy, communication, ensemble control, and presentation.
questions.learningOutcome: Use musical criteria to evaluate classroom and public performances.

questions.prompt: A group struggles with a fast passage. Which rehearsal plan is most effective?
options: Isolate the passage, practise slowly with steady pulse, then rebuild tempo
Repeat the whole piece faster each time without feedback
Skip the passage during every rehearsal
Ask only the strongest player to perform the entire piece
questions.correctAnswer: Isolate the passage, practise slowly with steady pulse, then rebuild tempo
questions.explanation: Focused slow practice helps accuracy before speed and ensemble flow are restored.
questions.learningOutcome: Select rehearsal strategies for solving technical and ensemble problems.

questions.prompt: A learner writes a 9/8 bar as two crotchets, one quaver, and one dotted crotchet. What is the problem?
options: The values add to eight quavers, so the bar is one quaver short
The values add to twelve quavers, so the bar is too long
The bar is correct because 9/8 allows any total
The dotted crotchet must always be silent
questions.correctAnswer: The values add to eight quavers, so the bar is one quaver short
questions.explanation: Two crotchets equal four quavers, plus one quaver and one dotted crotchet makes eight quavers, so the 9/8 bar is short by one quaver.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze compound-time notation for accurate bar values.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most strongly shows that a passage has modulated from C major to G major?
options: F sharp appears repeatedly and the phrase cadences on G
Middle C appears once in the melody
The tempo marking changes from andante to allegro
A rest occurs before the final bar
questions.correctAnswer: F sharp appears repeatedly and the phrase cadences on G
questions.explanation: A new leading note and a cadence in the new tonic give strong evidence of modulation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze melodic and harmonic evidence for key change.

questions.prompt: A melody in A minor needs a strong pull to the final A at a cadence. Which note choice helps most?
options: Use G sharp before the final A
Use G natural only before the final A
Avoid the note E in the phrase
Change the tonic from A to B flat
questions.correctAnswer: Use G sharp before the final A
questions.explanation: G sharp is the raised seventh in A harmonic minor and acts as the leading note to A.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how raised leading notes strengthen minor-key cadences.

questions.prompt: A composer wants the first four-bar phrase to ask a question rather than sound final. Which cadence is most suitable?
options: Imperfect cadence
Perfect cadence
Plagal cadence
Interrupted cadence followed by silence only
questions.correctAnswer: Imperfect cadence
questions.explanation: An imperfect cadence ends on the dominant and creates expectation for a responding phrase.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose cadences to shape antecedent and consequent phrases.

questions.prompt: In C major, which chords are represented by ii-V-I?
options: D minor, G major, C major
C major, F major, G major
A minor, D minor, E minor
G major, C major, F major
questions.correctAnswer: D minor, G major, C major
questions.explanation: The supertonic triad in C major is D minor, followed by dominant G major and tonic C major.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze functional chord progressions in major keys.

questions.prompt: Which chord is the secondary dominant V/V in C major?
options: D major
F major
A minor
E minor
questions.correctAnswer: D major
questions.explanation: V/V means the dominant of the dominant; in C major, the dominant is G, and D major is the dominant of G.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify applied dominant chords in simple tonal progressions.

questions.prompt: In a C major V-I cadence, the soprano has B over the G chord. Which resolution best follows tonal voice leading?
options: Move B up to C
Move B down to F
Keep B over the tonic chord
Leap B down to D sharp
questions.correctAnswer: Move B up to C
questions.explanation: B is the leading note in C major and normally resolves upward by step to the tonic.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze voice-leading choices at cadences.

questions.prompt: A melody moves C-D-E while the harmony remains C major and D falls on a weak part of the beat. What is D most likely acting as?
options: Passing note
Pedal point
Appoggiatura resolved by leap upward
New tonic
questions.correctAnswer: Passing note
questions.explanation: A passing note fills the stepwise space between two chord tones, often on a weaker part of the beat.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify passing notes and other non-chord tones in melodies.

questions.prompt: Which arrangement choice best supports a Kenyan fusion piece based on a pentatonic folk melody?
options: Keep the melody recognisable while adding an ostinato, drone, and sensitive harmonic colour
Replace the melody entirely with unrelated chromatic scales
Remove pulse and community context from the performance
Use only random sound effects with no structure
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the melody recognisable while adding an ostinato, drone, and sensitive harmonic colour
questions.explanation: A respectful fusion arrangement preserves identity while adding new textures and harmony carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze arrangement choices that preserve source identity while adding new musical material.

questions.prompt: Which description best indicates polyphonic texture?
options: Independent melodies are performed at the same time
All performers clap one identical rhythm only
A solo melody has block-chord accompaniment
The music contains no pitch
questions.correctAnswer: Independent melodies are performed at the same time
questions.explanation: Polyphony involves simultaneous independent melodic lines that interact with each other.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate homophonic, polyphonic, monophonic, and heterophonic textures.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports a reliable digital portfolio recording?
options: Plan takes, set input levels, record cleanly, label files, export, and reflect on improvements
Record once with clipping and delete the project file
Ignore microphone distance and export only silence
Rename every file the same way after mixing
questions.correctAnswer: Plan takes, set input levels, record cleanly, label files, export, and reflect on improvements
questions.explanation: A portfolio needs organized files, controlled recording levels, usable exports, and evidence of reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze production steps needed for a clear and assessable music portfolio.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to use a commercial beat in an original song for public posting. What is the safest legal choice?
options: Use a licensed beat or obtain permission before posting
Assume all online beats are free for any use
Hide the producer's name and post quickly
Change only the file name to avoid copyright
questions.correctAnswer: Use a licensed beat or obtain permission before posting
questions.explanation: Public use of copyrighted beats requires permission, a licence, or a clearly reusable source.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze copyright risks and choose lawful music-use options.

questions.prompt: Which sampling practice is most ethical when using a recorded community chant?
options: Seek consent, credit the source, respect context, and transform the sample responsibly
Use the recording secretly because it was easy to find
Remove the source details to make it seem original
Mock the chant to make the track more entertaining
questions.correctAnswer: Seek consent, credit the source, respect context, and transform the sample responsibly
questions.explanation: Ethical sampling considers permission, attribution, cultural meaning, and responsible creative use.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical choices when reusing recorded cultural material.

questions.prompt: Drums overpower singers in a dance performance. Which combined solution is most musical?
options: Adjust drum dynamics, staging, microphone gain, and arrangement density
Ask singers to shout through the whole piece
Remove all dancers from the stage
Ignore the issue because drums are always the main melody
questions.correctAnswer: Adjust drum dynamics, staging, microphone gain, and arrangement density
questions.explanation: Balance problems are solved through musical dynamics, space, amplification, and texture decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ensemble balance problems and recommend practical solutions.

questions.prompt: A composer repeats a short motif starting one step higher each time. Which development technique is being used?
options: Sequence
Inversion
Retrograde
Diminution
questions.correctAnswer: Sequence
questions.explanation: A sequence repeats a motif at a different pitch level, often stepwise or by a consistent interval.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze techniques used to develop melodic motifs.

questions.prompt: An eight-bar melody has a four-bar question phrase followed by a four-bar answering phrase. What structure does this show?
options: Antecedent and consequent phrase balance
Only a one-bar ostinato
A random sequence with no cadence
A twelve-bar blues pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Antecedent and consequent phrase balance
questions.explanation: Question and answer phrasing creates balanced antecedent and consequent units.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze phrase balance in original and studied melodies.

questions.prompt: Which instrument combination gives clear timbral contrast in a small Kenyan-inspired ensemble?
options: Voice, nyatiti, kayamba, and hand drum
Four identical recorders playing the same pitch only
Only two silent microphones
A choir with no rhythmic or melodic contrast
questions.correctAnswer: Voice, nyatiti, kayamba, and hand drum
questions.explanation: The combination contrasts vocal tone, string resonance, shaken idiophone colour, and drum timbre.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate instrumentation choices for colour, balance, and cultural fit.

questions.prompt: Which production plan best supports safety in a dance performance?
options: Check space, warm up, secure costumes, plan entrances, and manage hydration
Practise jumps on a slippery floor without warm-up
Block exits with props for dramatic effect
Use loose cables across the dancing area
questions.correctAnswer: Check space, warm up, secure costumes, plan entrances, and manage hydration
questions.explanation: Safe dance production manages bodies, space, costume, movement pathways, and backstage conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate performance plans for safety and stage readiness.

questions.prompt: Which programme-note content would best guide an audience listening to a classical movement?
options: Composer, period, form, main themes, and key listening features
Only the page number of the score
A list of unrelated football teams
The colour of the rehearsal room door
questions.correctAnswer: Composer, period, form, main themes, and key listening features
questions.explanation: Useful notes connect the music to context, structure, and what the audience can hear.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze information needed to support informed music listening.

questions.prompt: A DAW mix is clipping because the master meter goes above 0 dBFS. What should the producer do?
options: Lower track or bus levels and leave headroom before exporting
Raise every fader to make the distortion clearer
Add more tracks without adjusting gain
Export only the clipped section at a higher level
questions.correctAnswer: Lower track or bus levels and leave headroom before exporting
questions.explanation: Digital clipping causes distortion, so proper gain staging and headroom are needed before export.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze level problems in digital mixes and select corrective actions.

questions.prompt: A 16-bar song in C major must modulate smoothly to G major by bar 8. Which plan is strongest?
options: Use a shared chord such as C or Em, introduce F sharp, and cadence clearly in G
Jump randomly to E flat major without preparation
Avoid all cadences until the final bar
Use only percussion so the key cannot be heard
questions.correctAnswer: Use a shared chord such as C or Em, introduce F sharp, and cadence clearly in G
questions.explanation: A smooth modulation uses pivot material, the new leading note, and a cadence that confirms the new key.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a tonal plan that moves coherently between closely related keys.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves a four-part harmonisation with parallel fifths and awkward soprano leaps?
options: Rewrite inner voices for contrary motion and keep the soprano mostly stepwise within range
Double every leading note and keep all leaps
Move all voices in the same perfect fifths louder
Remove the bass line from every cadence
questions.correctAnswer: Rewrite inner voices for contrary motion and keep the soprano mostly stepwise within range
questions.explanation: Good revision protects voice independence, singable ranges, and smooth melodic motion.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate and improve four-part harmony for range, doubling, and voice leading.

questions.prompt: Which approach best creates a respectful jazz-influenced arrangement of a Kenyan folk tune?
options: Preserve the tune and function while adding tasteful reharmonisation, swing feel, and credited context
Replace the tune with unrelated jazz licks and hide the source
Use sacred text for comic effect without permission
Make every performer improvise in a different key
questions.correctAnswer: Preserve the tune and function while adding tasteful reharmonisation, swing feel, and credited context
questions.explanation: A strong fusion arrangement balances creativity with recognisable source material and respectful attribution.
questions.learningOutcome: Create arrangements that combine stylistic influence with source integrity.

questions.prompt: Which research plan is most suitable before documenting a community music practice?
options: Seek consent, record context accurately, translate key text, store files safely, and share findings respectfully
Record secretly and publish before asking questions
Write only personal guesses about the music
Collect names but ignore the function of the songs
questions.correctAnswer: Seek consent, record context accurately, translate key text, store files safely, and share findings respectfully
questions.explanation: Responsible research protects participants, context, data, and community relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Design ethical research methods for documenting music in society.

questions.prompt: A class ensemble includes beginners and advanced players. Which arrangement plan is most inclusive and musical?
options: Give differentiated parts that share the same pulse, form, and performance goal
Give only the advanced players all audible parts
Make beginners mime silently throughout
Change the tempo whenever a learner struggles
questions.correctAnswer: Give differentiated parts that share the same pulse, form, and performance goal
questions.explanation: Inclusive arranging lets learners contribute at suitable challenge levels while maintaining ensemble unity.
questions.learningOutcome: Create ensemble parts that support varied skill levels and shared musical purpose.

questions.prompt: A learner is designing a short game soundtrack cue for suspense. Which musical plan is most effective?
options: Use a minor mode, repeating ostinato, gradual dynamic build, and controlled dissonance
Use only a final perfect cadence at full volume from the first second
Avoid rhythm, texture, and contrast entirely
Use a cheerful major nursery melody with no variation
questions.correctAnswer: Use a minor mode, repeating ostinato, gradual dynamic build, and controlled dissonance
questions.explanation: Suspense can be shaped through mode, repetition, tension, texture, and dynamic growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Create musical cues that support mood and function in media contexts.

questions.prompt: A group learns that a song element planned for entertainment is sacred in its source community. What should they do?
options: Pause the use, seek guidance, and choose a permitted non-sacred alternative if needed
Use it more loudly because the audience may not know
Remove the community name and continue
Mock the sacred element to show originality
questions.correctAnswer: Pause the use, seek guidance, and choose a permitted non-sacred alternative if needed
questions.explanation: Respectful musicianship responds to cultural meaning and avoids misuse of restricted material.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate cultural restrictions and create respectful performance decisions.

questions.prompt: Which live sound plan is best for a small school concert with vocals, keyboard, guitar, and drums?
options: List inputs, set gain for each channel, place monitors safely, check feedback, and prepare backup cables
Use one overloaded microphone for every source
Skip sound check and adjust only after the concert
Point all speakers at the microphones to increase presence
questions.correctAnswer: List inputs, set gain for each channel, place monitors safely, check feedback, and prepare backup cables
questions.explanation: A reliable sound plan manages inputs, gain staging, monitoring, feedback risk, and contingency needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical sound reinforcement plans for school performance contexts.

questions.prompt: Which rubric would best assess a Grade 11 original composition?
options: Melody, rhythm, harmony, form, notation, creativity, performance feasibility, and reflection
Only how loudly the piece can be played
Only the number of pages in the score
Costume design and poster colour without musical criteria
questions.correctAnswer: Melody, rhythm, harmony, form, notation, creativity, performance feasibility, and reflection
questions.explanation: Composition assessment should balance technical craft, creativity, clarity, practical performance, and learner reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for evaluating original compositions fairly.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to release an original song professionally. Which plan is most production-ready?
options: Confirm ownership, register rights where applicable, prepare metadata, choose distribution, budget promotion, and track royalties
Upload an unlabeled file with no creator information
Use another artist's melody without permission
Ignore royalties because online music cannot earn income
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm ownership, register rights where applicable, prepare metadata, choose distribution, budget promotion, and track royalties
questions.explanation: Professional release planning combines legal ownership, accurate metadata, distribution choices, promotion, and income tracking.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a responsible plan for releasing and managing original music.
